+import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
+
+import type { TrpcSessionUser } from "../../../types";
+import { discardUnverifiedSignupHandler } from "./discardUnverifiedSignup.handler";
+
+const deleteMany = vi.fn();
+vi.mock("@calcom/features/di/containers/UserRepository", () => ({
+  getUserRepository: () => ({ deleteMany }),
+}));
+
+const makeCtx = (user: { emailVerified: Date | null; createdDate: Date }) => ({
+  user: { id: 7, ...user } as NonNullable<TrpcSessionUser>,
+});
+
+describe("discardUnverifiedSignupHandler", () => {
+  beforeEach(() => deleteMany.mockReset());
+
+  it("deletes a freshly created unverified account", async () => {
+    await discardUnverifiedSignupHandler({ ctx: makeCtx({ emailVerified: null, createdDate: new Date() }) });
+    expect(deleteMany).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ userIds: [7] });
+  });
+
+  it("refuses a verified account", async () => {
+    await expect(
+      discardUnverifiedSignupHandler({ ctx: makeCtx({ emailVerified: new Date(), createdDate: new Date() }) })
+    ).rejects.toThrow();
+    expect(deleteMany).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it("refuses an old unverified account", async () => {
+    const createdDate = new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
+    await expect(
+      discardUnverifiedSignupHandler({ ctx: makeCtx({ emailVerified: null, createdDate }) })
+    ).rejects.toThrow();
+    expect(deleteMany).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+});
diff --git a/packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/auth/discardUnverifiedSignup.handler.ts b/packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/auth/discardUnverifiedSignup.handler.ts

index 0000000000..93972fef6c
--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+import { getUserRepository } from "@calcom/features/di/containers/UserRepository";
+import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
+import type { TrpcSessionUser } from "../../../types";
+
+// Only accounts that were just created and never verified may be discarded, so an older
+// account that merely lacks verification can't be wiped through the "use different email" flow.
+const MAX_ACCOUNT_AGE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
+
+export const discardUnverifiedSignupHandler = async ({
+  ctx,
+}: {
+  ctx: { user: NonNullable<TrpcSessionUser> };
+}) => {
+  const { id, emailVerified, createdDate } = ctx.user;
+  if (emailVerified || Date.now() - new Date(createdDate).getTime() > MAX_ACCOUNT_AGE_MS) {
+    throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "Only a new, unverified account can be discarded" });
+  }
+
+  await getUserRepository().deleteMany({ userIds: [id] });
+  return { ok: true };
+};

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 21:58:33Z)**_

I added the toast. If someone clicks "Use a different email" more than 5 minutes after signing up, the server refuses to delete the account. The page now catches that refusal and shows a specific error toast instead of the generic "unexpected error" one:

> It's been more than 5 minutes since you signed up, so this account can no longer be changed. Please verify your email instead.

- **Code:** [verify-email-view.tsx:119-124](apps/web/modules/auth/verify-email-view.tsx#L119-L124) shows the new message when the error comes back as `FORBIDDEN`. Any other error still gets the generic toast.
- **Translation:** I added the new string as `use_different_email_expired` in [common.json](packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json).
- **Other changes:** Biome also reordered the imports in that file.

After the toast the user stays on the verify page, because they can no longer go back to the signup form. A `FORBIDDEN` error also comes back if the email is already verified, but the page redirects verified users away before they could click the button.

I haven't tried it in the browser and didn't add a test for the toast. The type check of `apps/web` still shows one error: `discardUnverifiedSignup` isn't found on the tRPC client. That comes from the previous commit, not this change, and should clear once the tRPC types are rebuilt (`cd packages/trpc && yarn build`). Nothing is committed.

- **Have vitest skip it:** add `".kilo/**"` to the exclude list in `vitest.config.ts` (the `getTestExclude()` call). That's a one-line change to repo config.

```typescript
import { getUserRepository } from "@calcom/features/di/containers/UserRepository";
import type { TrpcSessionUser } from "../../../types";

// Only accounts that were just created and never verified may be discarded, so an older
// account that merely lacks verification can't be wiped through the "use different email" flow.
const MAX_ACCOUNT_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

export const discardUnverifiedSignupHandler = async ({
  ctx,
}: {
  ctx: { user: NonNullable<TrpcSessionUser> };
}) => {
  const { id, emailVerified, createdDate } = ctx.user;
  // Returned rather than thrown: hitting the age limit is an expected outcome the UI explains,
  // and a thrown error would be logged as a console error by the client's tRPC logger.
  if (emailVerified || Date.now() - new Date(createdDate).getTime() > MAX_ACCOUNT_AGE_MS) {
    return { ok: false };
  }

  await getUserRepository().deleteMany({ userIds: [id] });
  return { ok: true };
};

```

The console error is gone. It appeared because tRPC's dev logger prints every failed request with `console.error`, and the handler was throwing a `FORBIDDEN` error when the account was too old. Next's dev overlay then showed that log as a "Console Error".

Running out of time isn't really a failure, so I made it a normal result instead:

- **Handler** ([discardUnverifiedSignup.handler.ts](packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/auth/discardUnverifiedSignup.handler.ts)): when the account is verified or more than 5 minutes old, it now returns `{ ok: false }` instead of throwing.
- **Verify-email page** ([verify-email-view.tsx](apps/web/modules/auth/verify-email-view.tsx)): if it gets `ok: false`, it shows the "more than 5 minutes" toast. Real failures still land in `catch` and show the generic error toast. I removed the `TRPCClientError` import, which is no longer needed.
- **Test**: the two "refuses" cases now expect `{ ok: false }` instead of an error. All 3 tests in the handler's test file pass and Biome reports nothing.

I haven't clicked through it in the browser to see the toast and confirm the overlay no longer appears.

I found why the toast never showed: the verify-email page had no `<Toaster />` on it. `showToast` only adds a toast to sonner's queue, and nothing on this page was there to display it. So no toast on this page could appear, not even the existing "Resend email" ones.

I added `<Toaster position="bottom-right" />` to [verify-email-view.tsx](apps/web/modules/auth/verify-email-view.tsx), the same way [verify-email-change-view.tsx](apps/web/modules/auth/verify-email-change-view.tsx) and the signup page do it. Biome passes.

I haven't checked it in the browser. To test it: sign up, wait more than 5 minutes, then click "Use a different email" in the same tab. The toast only fires when the saved signup data is still in that tab's session storage; in a different tab the button just signs you out.
